name: cobrowser
description: An embedded, agent-controllable browser inside your editor — co-driven by you (webview) and your AI agent (MCP).

cobrowser.chromePath.description: Path to the Chrome/Chromium executable. Leave empty to auto-detect.

cobrowser.headless.description: Run the browser headless — embedded in the Cursor panel only, with no separate OS window. Set to false to also open a native Chrome window (needed for native dropdowns, file pickers, 2FA, and some sign-ins like Google that block headless).

cobrowser.port.description: Localhost port for the in-process MCP server. 0 (default) = pick a free port automatically and remember it per-workspace, so every window/repo gets its own stable endpoint and two windows never collide (which would make agents drive each other's browsers). Set a specific number only to pin a port for one workspace.

enumDescriptions: Lossy, lighter frames. Slight ringing around text on close inspection.
Lossless — pixel-perfect text, no compression artifacts ever.
cobrowser.imageFormat.description: Frame format for the browser stream. Measured while scrolling at 3.1Mpx: on text-heavy pages PNG is lossless AND slightly smaller than JPEG q90 (457KB vs 478KB per frame) at 41 vs 46fps; on photo-heavy pages PNG doubles the bytes (780KB vs 375KB) at similar frame rate. Bandwidth is not the bottleneck, so this is mostly 'perfect text' vs 'lighter frames'. Applies immediately.

enumDescriptions: Chromium as a local child process. Instant start, shared macOS profile, no dependencies. Frame rate is capped ~45fps by Chromium's own capture path.

Chromium inside a Docker container, captured from its X11 framebuffer. Measured ~248fps of changed frames — bypasses Chromium's capture ceiling. Requires Docker; the browser profile is separate from the local one.
cobrowser.backend.description: Where the browser runs. 'container' trades a Docker dependency and a separate browser profile for a large frame-rate increase, because Chromium's own capture path (both startScreencast and captureScreenshot) tops out near 45fps while the page renders at 80.

cobrowser.containerWidth.description: Container display width in pixels. The page fills this exactly (the panel letterboxes to fit), so pick something near your panel's aspect ratio. Applied on browser restart.

cobrowser.containerHeight.description: Container display height in pixels. Applied on browser restart.

cobrowser.containerFps.description: Frame capture rate inside the container. Only CHANGED frames are sent (a still page costs nothing), so this is a ceiling rather than a constant load.

cobrowser.videoPipeline.description: EXPERIMENTAL: render panels via hardware H.264 video (WebCodecs tab-capture) instead of per-frame JPEG — ~100x less bandwidth and near-zero CPU, smoother under motion. Panels fall back to the JPEG screencast automatically if capture fails. Takes effect when a panel next starts streaming (hide/show it, or reload).

cobrowser.uncapFrameRate.description: Remove headless Chrome's 60fps compositor cap so panels stream at up to ~90-100fps (the JPEG-encode ceiling). COSTLY: pages that animate via requestAnimationFrame will render thousands of frames per second internally (measured ~6800), pegging CPU and draining battery — leave off unless plugged in and chasing maximum smoothness. Takes effect after 'Cobrowser: Restart Browser'.

cobrowser.autoFallbackPasskeys.description: Install a virtual WebAuthn authenticator so passkey/WebAuthn prompts fail fast and sites fall back to a password. Headless Chromium can't show the OS fingerprint prompt, so a passkey ceremony would otherwise hang forever. Turn OFF only when running headful (cobrowser.headless: false) to sign in with the real OS prompt.
